name: Arambourgiania
sum: Giant azhdarchid from Maastrichtian phosphates of Jordan, known chiefly from an enormous neck vertebra originally mistaken for a wing bone.
wsnote: Early estimates of 11–13 m are now considered too high; recent estimates range from about 8–9 m (Paul 2022) to about 10 m (2024 study). 7 m has also been proposed.
holotype: Holotype cervical vertebra (originally ~61 cm long) — phosphate mines near Russeifa, Jordan; found 1943.
material: Incomplete neck vertebra; fragmentary material possibly from the same individual (metacarpal, femur, cervical fragments) described in 2018.
biology: Like other azhdarchids, probably a terrestrial stalker feeding on small animals; known from a coastal marine setting.
author: Nessov et al. 1987
